55169fa8892d.title: Junior Mechanical Engineer (Summer 2026)
55169fa8892d.description:
About Us
You rarely get the chance to change an entire industry. But that's the position we find ourselves in. Join us, and you’ll unleash scientists, accelerate their research and help get cures to patients sooner.
 
We’ve developed machines to fully automate human cell production - the most manual process in Biotech. Cells are used to discover and develop new drugs, and now they're being used to treat cancer too. Mytos will impact cure development across the board.
 
We're live in multibillion dollar biotechs on both coasts of the US, and just raised $19m to expand into the market faster, and accelerate our development!
 
We’ve assembled a world-class team to take on this challenge, with ex-Dyson engineers and Nature-published scientists working hand-in-hand. You can learn more about your potential Mytos teammates here: Team
 
Mytos is backed by Y Combinator, the most successful startup program in the world which produced companies such as AirBnb, Dropbox, and Ginkgo Bioworks. 
 
 We’re building a team that enjoys moving fast and not killing cells, strives for continuous improvement through learning from mistakes and is passionate about work that contributes to solving real world problems. 
 
We get excited about meeting potential colleagues from broad scientific/engineering backgrounds and who share our enthusiasm for unconstrained innovation and understanding our users.
 Working in the HW team to develop solutions to be incorporated in our systems
 Having the freedom to suggest ways to refine existing designs, and how we source and manufacture parts
 Understanding user goals and user journeys, and incorporating them into continuously improving product design
 Assembling, testing and validating complex devices
 Multi-disciplinary collaboration across the whole team, which includes two Forbes 30 under 30 founders, ex-Dyson engineers, rock climbers and Nature-published scientists We believe that as a mechanical engineer, you’d be hard pressed to find a more interesting and impactful problem to work on. We’d love to hear from you if you think you would enjoy: An educational background in Mechanical Engineering, with an interest in product and user centred design
 Some related work experience or internships. We’re especially excited to meet potential colleagues with exposure to the fields of lab automation, medical devices, and robotics, with a keen interest in thermodynamics, fluidics, and control systems
 Experience with at least one CAD package (Solidworks preferable) You Bring: Competitive salary with stock options
 Lunch covered daily
 Collaborative team environment with very high potential to learn new skills
 24 days holiday (excluding bank holidays)
 Pension
 Awesome colleagues and an office in the Imperial College Innovation hub in White City, where you’ll be based.
 Because of the device assembly aspect of this role, we are unable to support remote-first working and potential colleagues must be happy to work from our lab. Salary and Benefits:

b865cea7b3f2.title: Associate, Client Services (January 2027 Start)
b865cea7b3f2.description:
Third Bridge is a leading global research firm established in 2007, with a team of over 1,500 employees worldwide dedicated to fueling decisions with expert insights . We accelerate and enhance decision-making for investors and business leaders by unearthing unique expert insights across multiple sectors, geographies, and topics.
 For nearly 20 years, we’ve helped clients access knowledge on demand from experts, in-person and through our Library covering over 65,000 companies.
 Start Dates:  January & April 2027
 Want to  accelerate your career  in a  high-energy, commercial role?  If you’re competitive, a confident communicator, both on the phone and in person, and  hungry to grow fast , our  Associate role at Third Bridge could be your next big move.
 Job Description
 Why Join Us? 
 We’re offering more than a role - we’re offering a  career launchpad . As a Client Services Associate, you’ll develop the  commercial awareness  and  business acumen  that open doors to long-term careers in  sales, account management, leadership , research and so much more. We  promote from within , and our top performers move into management in as little as two years.
 You’ll thrive if you:
 Love a  fast-paced, target-driven  environment
 Have the  confidence to pick up the phone  and start conversations with anyone
 Are naturally curious, quick to learn and love to  solve complex problems 
 Build rapport fast and think on your feet
 Are resilient and motivated to  exceed goals 
 What You’ll Do 
 You’ll be at the heart of our business - finding, calling, and engaging industry experts to deliver the insights our clients need, often under  extremely tight deadlines.  Expect to spend much of your day on the phone, persuading specialists to share their expertise and securing their time for client calls. 
 Day to day, you’ll:
 Own projects end-to-end , truly understanding the specific client needs and scheduling high-calibre expert calls.
 Cold call  and engage experts across industries, overcoming objections and winning buy-in
 Work at speed, managing  multiple projects and clients  at once
 Learn fast , gaining broad knowledge of markets, business models, and regulations
 Cross-Sell  the full range of Third Bridge services including content library, surveys, advisory, as well as 1-1 calls.
 What You’ll Gain 
 Commercial edge:  Sales, negotiation, relationship-building skills and the opportunity to develop leadership skills very early in your career
 Client exposure:  Work with leading private equity firms, hedge funds, and consultancies
 Clear progression:  Every manager started in the Associate role; promotion possible within 2 years
 Annual  Personal Development Allowance  to invest in your growth
 Would you like to learn more about our Associate position? Take our free  virtual job simulation and learn what it is like to work in this role. 
 Qualifications
 What We’re Looking For 
 You’re  intellectually strong , you’re  ambitious , have  leadership or extracurricular experience , and have shown grit through internships, work experience, or other achievements.
 Additional Information
 Salary and Benefits: 
 Total first-year salary is expected to be  £51,000–£68,000  (based on average-high performance). This is in line with a  £40,000 base salary  plus an  uncapped performance bonus  accessible after your first month.
 Enjoy  comprehensive benefits  including health, dental, vision, pension contributions, and more.
 Appreciate good work-life balance with 25+ vacation days,  flex days , and  work from anywhere for one month per year 
 Be part of our  engaging culture  with social events, professional development, and a dynamic, supportive team.

 We are seeking highly motivated candidates who are enthusiastic about making a difference to children's mental health through evidence-based interventions based on NICE Guideline recommended treatment.

 Graduate Quantity Surveyor - 2027 Development Programme - UK Wide 
 We're excited to open applications for our 2027 Graduate Programme, starting in September. This is your opportunity to build a meaningful career where your work contributes to healthier, greener, and more inclusive places for people to thrive.
 Over two years, you'll gain hands-on experience, structured learning, and the support of mentors who care about your growth. You'll develop the technical and interpersonal skills to help you succeed and make a lasting impact.

 Assist with contract administration and commercial reporting.
 Accurately input and manage data in contract management systems.
 Certify and process contract change control by logging change notices, obtaining approvals and quantifying cost/time impacts.
 Keep detailed cost ledgers, reconcile site and procurement records and assist in cost negotiation and agreement with subcontractors.
 Actively engage with the Skanska Graduate Programme for professional development towards chartered status.

 Degree in Quantity Surveying, Construction Commercial Management or equivalent (RICS accredited).
 Familiarity with commercial IT systems (e.g., Oracle, CEMAR, ProjectWise) and proficiency with spreadsheets for costing, data manipulation and basic modelling.
 Solid understanding of measurement and estimating (take-offs, cost checks, bills of quantities or schedule of rates) and awareness of contract variation, notices and claims processes.
 Clear written and verbal communication, strong attention to detail, team-working mindset and active pursuit of professional accreditation.
 This role requires visits to sites across the UK. As such, we would expect you to have a driving licence or work towards obtaining one within your first year of working with us.

Job Title: Locum Speech and Language Therapist – Adult Acute Inpatients – South Wales
 Banding: Band 6/7
 Location: South Wales
 Start Date: ASAP
 Rate: £24.00–£31.00 per hour
 Working Hours: Full-time or Part-time Available
 Contract Duration: 3 Months
 Job Overview
 We are currently seeking a skilled and motivated Speech and Language Therapist to join an Adult Acute team in South Wales on a locum basis. This exciting opportunity involves working across inpatient services, supporting adults with a range of communication and swallowing difficulties arising from acute medical conditions.
 This role is suitable for an experienced Band 6 Speech and Language Therapist looking to broaden their acute experience or a Band 7 clinician seeking a flexible locum opportunity within a supportive multidisciplinary environment. You will play a key role in assessing, diagnosing, and managing patients with complex speech, language, communication, and swallowing needs, helping to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care.
 Key Responsibilities
 In this role, you will:
 • Assess, diagnose, and manage adults presenting with communication and swallowing disorders within acute inpatient services.
• Deliver evidence-based interventions for patients with dysphagia, acquired communication disorders, cognitive-communication difficulties, and neurological conditions.
• Undertake comprehensive swallowing assessments and provide appropriate management plans to support safe nutrition and hydration.
• Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams including medical staff, nursing teams, dietitians, occupational therapists, and physiotherapists.
• Participate in ward rounds, case discussions, and discharge planning meetings.
• Maintain accurate and up-to-date clinical records in accordance with professional and organisational standards.
• Provide advice, education, and support to patients, families, carers, and healthcare professionals.
• Contribute to service development initiatives and support junior colleagues where appropriate.
 Qualifications and Experience
 To be considered for this role, you must have:
 • A recognised degree in Speech and Language Therapy (or equivalent).
• Current HCPC registration.
• Membership of the Royal College of Speech and Language Therapists (RCSLT).
• Previous experience working within adult acute inpatient services.
• Experience managing patients with dysphagia and complex communication needs.
• Excellent clinical reasoning, communication, and organisational skills.
• The ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a multidisciplinary team.
 Why Choose Pulse?

c721c4a7b622.description:
Job Title: Adult Neuro Community Speech and Language Therapist
 Banding: Band 6 / 7
 Location: Southampton
 Start Date: ASAP
 Rate: £25.00 – £32.00 per hour
 Working Hours: Full time / Part time
 Working Style: Hybrid – combination of essential face-to-face patient visits, office-based meetings, and remote clinical administration
 Job Overview
 We are seeking a skilled and enthusiastic Adult Neuro Speech and Language Therapist to join a community-based neurorehabilitation service in Southampton. This hybrid role requires regular face-to-face visits to patients in their homes , complemented by occasional office-based meetings and remote clinical administration. Staff may choose to attend the office more frequently if preferred.
 The role is ideal for a Band 6 or Band 7 therapist experienced in adult neurorehabilitation or looking to develop specialist skills. You will be part of the Neuro Early Supported Discharge (ESD) team, providing intensive neurorehabilitation to adults with stroke or other neurological conditions who are newly discharged from hospital or at risk of hospital admission. The team covers Southampton City and parts of West Hampshire.
 Important: Access to a car is required, as the role involves travel to patient homes across Southampton, the New Forest, Hamble, Andover, and Fordingbridge. Car insurance must cover business use. A Trust laptop, work phone, Smartcard, and System One access are essential for the role.
 Key Responsibilities
 In this role, you will:
 Conduct regular face-to-face assessments and interventions with clients in their homes or community settings.
 Work as part of a multi-professional neurorehabilitation team, collaborating with acute rehabilitation units, community rehab teams, inpatient wards, and rapid response services.
 Manage a caseload of clients in community or ward settings, including oversight of rehabilitation assistants.
 Assess and treat clients with complex or chronic neurological conditions, determining both profession-specific and multidisciplinary rehabilitation interventions.
 Plan and implement comprehensive programmes of intensive rehabilitation in hospital, clinic, or community settings.
 Support team operations by managing caseloads during team leader absence, attending MDT meetings, scheduling work, and providing specialist advice.
 Perform specialist and general multidisciplinary rehabilitation procedures requiring advanced clinical knowledge.
 Mentor and support junior staff, rehabilitation assistants, and students on clinical placement.
 Maintain and develop professional skills through CPD, including participation in professional special interest groups and integration of new developments into practice.
 Contribute actively to team development initiatives.
 Qualifications and Experience
 To be considered for this role, you must have:
 A recognised degree in Speech and Language Therapy (or equivalent).
 HCPC registration and eligibility for membership of the Royal College of Speech and Language Therapists (RCSLT).
 Experience or a strong interest in adult neurorehabilitation and working with complex neurological presentations.
 Excellent communication, organisation, and interpersonal skills.
 Flexibility to travel and deliver regular face-to-face patient visits across Southampton and West Hampshire.
 A proactive, collaborative, and reflective approach to professional practice.

 Contributing to clinical governance, quality improvement and service evaluation.

 Applicants must possess:
 Basic medical qualification.
 MRCP (UK), MRCP Gastroenterology or equivalent postgraduate qualification.
 Full GMC registration with a licence to practise, together with inclusion on the GMC Specialist Register in Gastroenterology, or eligibility for specialist registration within six months of the interview date.

 Higher degree (MD, PhD or equivalent).

 Essential
 Broad clinical experience across gastroenterology and hepatology.

 Demonstrable commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion within clinical practice.

 Wider experience gained both within and outside the specialty.

 Transnasal Endoscopy

 Essential
 Evidence of commitment to undergraduate and postgraduate medical education.
 Desirable
 Formal teaching or educational qualification.

 Essential
 Evidence of participation in clinical audit and quality improvement activities.
 Desirable
 Research experience.
 Peer-reviewed publications.
 Academic achievements, prizes or honours.

11beef3c47ff.description:
Opportunity 
 An excellent fixed term or permanent opportunity has arisen within the Orthopaedic department at an NHS Foundation Trust serving the community of West Norfolk and the surrounding region. We are seeking an experienced Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon with a subspecialty interest and expertise in Upper Limb surgery to join our established and friendly team.
 This fixed term post offers a substantive clinical workload across elective upper limb surgery and trauma, with the opportunity to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care within a supportive orthopaedic department. The post would suit a candidate looking to consolidate or develop their upper limb practice in an NHS environment, whether returning to the NHS, relocating, or seeking a defined-term appointment.
 The post includes a generous Supporting Professional Activities (SPA) allocation, flexible job planning, and a structured on-call commitment proportionate to a fixed term appointment. We are committed to supporting all colleagues – permanent and fixed term alike – to feel fully integrated and valued members of the department from day one.
 Pulse Doctors welcome applications from candidates at any stage of their consultant career, including those who are newly appointed, returning to practice, or seeking a time-limited role in a high-quality district general hospital setting in West Norfolk.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Elective Upper Limb Surgery 
 Provide consultant-led elective upper limb surgical services, including shoulder, elbow, wrist and hand surgery, in line with the post-holder’s subspecialty expertise.
 Lead and conduct elective upper limb outpatient clinics, including new patient assessment, post-operative review, and injection therapy.
 Undertake elective upper limb procedures including arthroplasty, arthroscopy, tendon and soft tissue reconstruction, carpal tunnel and nerve decompression, and fracture management as appropriate.
 Contribute to the development and optimisation of upper limb pathways, including referral management and waiting list initiatives.
 Work collaboratively with physiotherapy, hand therapy, and occupational therapy colleagues to deliver comprehensive upper limb rehabilitation.
 Trauma & Emergency Orthopaedics 
 Participate in the orthopaedic trauma on-call rota, providing consultant-level decision-making and operative cover for acute upper limb and general orthopaedic trauma.
 Contribute to the fracture clinic service, including assessment and management of upper limb fractures and dislocations.
 Provide clinical oversight and support to junior colleagues managing acute orthopaedic presentations in the emergency department and on the wards.
 Engage with the trauma MDT, including liaison with emergency medicine, radiology, anaesthetics, and therapy colleagues.
 Leadership, Education & Governance 
 Participate in departmental clinical governance, audit, morbidity & mortality review, and quality improvement activity.
 Contribute to the teaching and supervision of specialty trainees, core surgical trainees, and other clinical staff.
 Engage with the orthopaedic MDT and relevant regional networks, including upper limb and hand surgery networks where applicable.
 Support departmental initiatives to improve patient outcomes, theatre efficiency, and elective recovery.
 Maintain and develop clinical expertise in line with BOA and relevant subspecialty society CPD requirements.
 Essential Criteria to Apply 
 Qualifications & Registration 
 Full registration with the General Medical Council (GMC) with a licence to practise.
 Entry on the GMC Specialist Register in Trauma & Orthopaedic Surgery, or within six months of eligibility at the time of interview.
 FRCS (Tr & Orth) or equivalent specialist qualification.
 Completion of a recognised higher surgical training programme or equivalent, with demonstrable upper limb subspecialty training or experience.
 Clinical Experience & Skills 
 Demonstrable surgical competence across a range of upper limb procedures appropriate to a DGH consultant post, including shoulder and/or elbow arthroplasty, arthroscopic surgery, and soft tissue reconstruction.
 Experience in the management of acute upper limb trauma, including fractures, dislocations, and tendon injuries.
 Ability to contribute independently to the orthopaedic on-call rota from the start of the appointment.
 Evidence of engagement with clinical audit, governance, and quality improvement in an orthopaedic context.
 Experience of working within or contributing to an MDT environment involving physiotherapy, hand therapy, and radiology colleagues.
 Personal Attributes 
 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build confidence and trust with patients and colleagues.
 A motivated, adaptable and collaborative approach, with the ability to integrate quickly and effectively into an established team.
 Commitment to delivering high-quality, safe and patient-centred surgical care.
 Enthusiasm for contributing to a district general hospital and the community it serves.
 Commitment to equality, diversity, and inclusion in all aspects of clinical practice and team working.
 What’s on Offer for You? 
 Permanent or fixed-term salaried NHS Consultant contract: £113,565 - £150,569 (Depending on Experience) 
 Flexible job planning: we will work with you to develop a job plan that reflects your clinical expertise and the needs of the department.
 Generous SPA allocation to support CPD, audit, teaching, and professional development throughout the duration of the contract.
 Defined and manageable on-call commitment as part of a well-supported orthopaedic rota.Dedicated Study Leave budget and support for BOA and subspecialty society CPD requirements.
 Access to staff wellbeing services, an employee assistance programme, and health and fitness facilities.
 Full access to departmental education, simulation, and governance activity from the outset.
 A welcoming and supportive orthopaedic team with a strong collaborative culture.
 Location in Detail 
 This post is based in West Norfolk, a distinctive and rewarding part of England that offers an exceptional quality of life alongside a fulfilling clinical career.
 West Norfolk is a largely rural and coastal county, home to dramatic landscapes including the Norfolk Coast Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, the Broads, and miles of unspoilt beaches. The area is well known for its strong sense of community, low crime rates, and significantly lower cost of living compared to London and the South East.
 Local towns offer excellent schools (state and independent), a vibrant arts and culture scene, and outstanding outdoor pursuits including sailing, cycling, horse riding and walking. The region is also renowned for its food and drink – from fresh seafood to award-winning local produce.
 Transport links are good, with direct rail connections to Cambridge and London Liverpool Street, making the area accessible for those with ties to the city. Norwich, the county city of Norfolk, is approximately 45 minutes by road and offers further retail, dining, and cultural amenities.
 For candidates considering a fixed term relocation, West Norfolk offers an outstanding base – whether for a defined chapter of your career, a return to NHS practice, or a period of professional consolidation – in a region that is genuinely hard to leave.
 About Pulse Healthcare Doctors 
 Pulse Healthcare Doctors is a leading medical recruitment partner, supporting NHS Trusts and private healthcare
organisations across the UK. We work closely with hospitals to connect talented doctors with outstanding permanent and
fixed-term career opportunities.
 To discuss this opportunity in confidence or to submit your application, please contact Stuart on the email address:
stuart.sutherland@pulsejobs.com

 Obstetrics
•    Provide consultant-led care across the full range of obstetric conditions, including antenatal, intrapartum and postnatal services.
•    Lead and participate in high-risk obstetric clinics, including maternal medicine and fetal medicine, in line with departmental responsibilities.
•    Take a proactive role in the delivery suite as part of the on-call and resident obstetric rota.
•    Provide clinical leadership for the multidisciplinary obstetric team, including midwives, anaesthetists and neonatal colleagues.
•    Contribute to the management of obstetric emergencies, with a commitment to simulation training and skills-and-drills programmes.
 Gynaecology
    Provide a comprehensive outpatient gynaecology service, including general gynaecology, early pregnancy, and any agreed subspecialty clinics.
•    Undertake elective and emergency gynaecological surgery, with competence across the core procedural repertoire expected of an NHS O&G consultant.
•    Participate in the gynaecology on-call rota, covering acute gynaecological emergencies and supporting junior colleagues.
•    Contribute to the development and delivery of benign gynaecology, including minimally invasive approaches where appropriate.
•    Engage with the gynaecological oncology pathway, working closely with regional cancer networks and MDT processes.

    Full registration with the General Medical Council (GMC) with a licence to practise.

•    Demonstrable experience across the breadth of obstetrics and gynaecology at consultant or senior registrar level.
•    Competence in the operative and procedural skills expected of an NHS O&G consultant, including obstetric emergencies and gynaecological surgery.

2a48899f65dc.title: Substantive Consultant – Obstetrics & Gynaecology - West Norfolk
2a48899f65dc.description:
Opportunity 
At Pulse Doctors, we are delighted to be working in partnership with an leading hospital in West Norfolk to recruit an enthusiastic, motivated and clinically excellent Consultant in Obstetrics and Gynaecology to complement a established and friendly team. This post offers a rewarding breadth of clinical work across both obstetrics and gynaecology, with real scope to develop subspecialty interests in line with departmental need and your own professional goals.
The Trust is committed to the wellbeing and professional development of its consultants. The post includes a generous Supporting Professional Activities (SPA) allocation, structured on-call commitment, and flexible job planning to support a sustainable and fulfilling career. Full-time and less-than-full-time applicants are equally welcome.
This is a genuine opportunity to be part of a close-knit, high-performing team that takes pride in delivering excellent, personalised care to the women and families of West Norfolk.
 Key Responsibilities 
Obstetrics
•    Provide consultant-led care across the full range of obstetric conditions, including antenatal, intrapartum and postnatal services.
•    Lead and participate in high-risk obstetric clinics, including maternal medicine and fetal medicine, in line with departmental responsibilities.
•    Take a proactive role in the delivery suite as part of the on-call and resident obstetric rota.
•    Provide clinical leadership for the multidisciplinary obstetric team, including midwives, anaesthetists and neonatal colleagues.
•    Contribute to the management of obstetric emergencies, with a commitment to simulation training and skills-and-drills programmes.
Gynaecology
 •    Provide a comprehensive outpatient gynaecology service, including general gynaecology, early pregnancy, and any agreed subspecialty clinics.
•    Undertake elective and emergency gynaecological surgery, with competence across the core procedural repertoire expected of an NHS O&G consultant.
•    Participate in the gynaecology on-call rota, covering acute gynaecological emergencies and supporting junior colleagues.
•    Contribute to the development and delivery of benign gynaecology, including minimally invasive approaches where appropriate.
•    Engage with the gynaecological oncology pathway, working closely with regional cancer networks and MDT processes.
 Essential Criteria to Apply 
•    Full registration with the General Medical Council (GMC) with a licence to practise.
•    Entry on the GMC Specialist Register in Obstetrics & Gynaecology, or within six months of eligibility at the time of interview.
•    MRCOG or equivalent specialist qualification in Obstetrics & Gynaecology.
•    Completion of a recognised O&G training programme or equivalent.
•    Demonstrable experience across the breadth of obstetrics and gynaecology at consultant or senior registrar level.
•    Competence in the operative and procedural skills expected of an NHS O&G consultant, including obstetric emergencies and gynaecological surgery.
•    Experience in managing high-risk pregnancy and complex gynaecological conditions.
•    Ability to work independently as a consultant and contribute effectively to the on-call rota.
•    Evidence of engagement with clinical governance, audit, and quality improvement.
 What’s on Offer for You? 
•    Permanent or fixed-term salaried NHS Consultant contract: £113,565 - £150,569 (Depending on Experience).
•    Flexible job planning: we will work collaboratively with you to develop a job plan that reflects your clinical interests and personal circumstances, whether full-time or less-than-full-time.
•    Generous SPA allocation to support CPD, audit, research, teaching, and leadership activity.
•    Defined and manageable on-call commitment as part of a collegial and well-supported rota.
•    NHS Pension Scheme – one of the most comprehensive pension arrangements available in the UK.
•    Relocation assistance available for eligible candidates.
•    Dedicated Study Leave budget and support for RCOG CEPD requirements.
•    Access to staff wellbeing services, an employee assistance programme, and health and fitness facilities.
•    Opportunities to develop and lead subspecialty interests, including within regional networks.
•    A supportive, stable and welcoming department with a strong team culture.
 Location in Detail 
This post is based in West Norfolk, a distinctive and rewarding part of England that offers an exceptional quality of life alongside a fulfilling clinical career.
West Norfolk is a largely rural and coastal county, home to dramatic landscapes including the Norfolk Coast Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, the Broads, and miles of unspoilt beaches. The area is well known for its strong sense of community, low crime rates, and significantly lower cost of living compared to London and the South East.
 Local towns offer excellent schools (state and independent), a vibrant arts and culture scene, and outstanding outdoor pursuits including sailing, cycling, horse riding and walking. The region is also renowned for its food and drink – from fresh seafood to award-winning local produce.
Transport links are good, with direct rail connections to Cambridge and London Liverpool Street, making the area accessible for those with ties to the city. Norwich, the county city of Norfolk, is approximately 45 minutes by road and offers further retail, dining, and cultural amenities.
For candidates considering relocation, West Norfolk offers an outstanding place to raise a family, enjoy a calmer pace of life, or pursue interests outside of medicine – without compromising on professional challenge or career progression.
 About Pulse Healthcare Doctors 
Pulse Healthcare Doctors is a leading medical recruitment partner, supporting NHS Trusts and private healthcare organisations across the UK. We work closely with hospitals to connect talented doctors with outstanding permanent and fixed-term career opportunities.
 To discuss this opportunity in confidence or to submit your application, please contact Stuart on the email address: stuart.sutherland@pulsejobs.com

Children's Wellbeing Practitioner Trainee
 Job Introduction HCRG Care Group are looking to recruit Children's Wellbeing Practitioners to continue to improve children and young people's mental health services in Essex.
 This is a training position where you will undertake training through Anna Freud alongside working in our Essex Child and Family Wellbeing Services.
 The Children's Wellbeing Practitioner (CWP) role has been developed by NHS England as part of the Children and Young People's Psychological Trainings (formerly CYP Improving Access to Psychological Therapies - CYP IAPT) programme.
 The course focuses on working within community and primary care settings to increase access to support for children, young people and families. You'll be trained as a CWP to offer evidence-based interventions like low intensity support and guided self-help.
 This course enables you to support children and young people with mild to moderate:
 Anxiety (working with primary and secondary school pupils, parents and carers)
 Low mood (adolescents)
 Common behavioural difficulties (working with parents and carers).
 Applicants will need to be ready to start work in early-mid January 2027. Positions cannot be offered to candidates unless they are available for the start date.
 Please note that applications for this position is a dual process. Prospective candidates must apply to the university course at the same time as application to this role. A standard recruitment process will follow, with our shortlisted candidate information being shared with the university. The university will check their application portal, confirm candidates' course eligibility and report this to the service. The service will create a final shortlist with this information and will offer to the applicant successful at the job interview (subject to final university checks).
 You will need a Driving license and use of vehicle for work purposes 
 Package Description 
 You will feel valued as a Children's Wellbeing Practitioner Trainee within HCRG Care Group, receiving access to exclusive rewards and benefits including:
 A salary of £28,500 with access to our group pension
 Free tea, coffee and milk at your base location
 Membership of My Reward Hub, giving you access to discounts on every day purchases like grocery shopping as well as cashback and voucher offers for treats for you and those special to you
 Access to your wages as you earn them to help cover life's emergencies and avoid overdraft fees or high interest rates
 Online and face to face help with your mental and physical wellbeing - from healthy recipes and activity challenges through to post trauma support, legal, debt and life management help, as well career coaching and counselling
 Access to eLearning, bespoke career pathways and opportunities for continuing professional development through our 'Outstanding' learning and development team, The Learning Enterprise
 An open, just culture where you're encouraged to have and implement ideas which can help us deliver our purpose: changing lives through transforming health and care - backed up by at least £100,000 of ringfenced innovation funding each year
 Main Responsibilities We are seeking to recruit 2 graduate level practitioners to provide guided self-help therapy and parenting interventions .
 These posts are fully funded for a one year.
 You will learn:
 Evidence-based and collaborative practice
 Availability and awareness of evidence-based interventions
 Goal-focused, client-centred interventions using feedback tools to facilitate collaboration between professionals, young people and families, leading to more personalised care
 Giving children, young people and families a voice and influence
 Cross-agency collaboration between health, social care, voluntary and independent sectors
 Working with partner organisations to reduce stigma of mental health and improve understanding of the importance of emotional wellbeing
 Making services accountable by monitoring and sharing outcome data with young people, families and commissioners.
 Be trained to offer consultations and training to colleagues from partner agencies.
 Be introduced to a range of outcome and feedback measures used in CYP Psychological Trainings (PT), and review and interpret them with children, young people, parents and carers
 Develop an understanding of the core principles of participation and collaboration, and learn how to integrate this into your work.
 Assessment:
 You'll be assessed through presentations, reflective analysis, a poster, a case report and video clips of your clinical practice.
 This programme emphasises putting skills into practice and consolidating learning.
 You will develop a portfolio of a range of case work over the year, aiming for a minimum of 30 pieces of case work.
 The post holder will attend all university based taught and self-study days required by the education provider, as specified within the agreed national curriculum and work in the service for the remaining days of the week using their newly developed skills.
 The PgDip CWP training programme will take place over 12 months. 
*There are approximately 64 teaching days in the year, split between three terms:
 Term one: three days per week
 Term two: two days per week
 Term three: one day per week
 During university holidays, you're expected to work full time in your service. Trainees will have the usual annual leave allocation in line with HCRG Care Group Policy.

 For any queries related to the role please contact the hiring team at 
 Ideal candidates will:
 Second-class or higher bachelor's degree from a UK university in a relevant subject (e.g. psychology, education, childhood development, social work)
 An overseas qualification of an equivalent standard in a relevant subject
 Degree in any subject with further training or experience in a relevant field (e.g. teaching, TA, learning support, HCA, youth work, counselling).

Our Company
At Quantum, we connect global brands with high-intent consumers. We turn intent into action and complexity into clarity.



Our Mission is clear, to help smarter, faster buying decisions. Our vision, to be the world’s most used digital comparison service, delivering value and simplicity to millions.



We drive growth through data-driven affiliate marketing built for performance from day one. Every campaign is measurable, optimised in real time, and designed to scale.



With in-house tech, full-stack analytics, and a compliance-first mindset, we give our partners an edge. We drive confident decisions and growth in regulated and high-growth sectors. We’ve helped ambitious brands grow faster, smarter, and globally.



The Role

Our Commercial Insights team is growing! We're looking for a Graduate Commercial Insights

Analyst to join our team in London.

This is where an analytics career starts. You'll learn how a high-growth business really runs on data, working alongside experienced analysts on the numbers that shape commercial decisions.

 - Learn the full Quantum data stack, from Hightouch to BigQuery and GA4 through to Tableau

 - Be on the front line building out innovative Ai-led solutions using Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT

 - Get hands-on with making meaningful recommendations using real business data from week one

 - See your analysis drive real outcomes within the commercial, marketing, and product teams

 - Build the foundations to grow into a Commercial Insights Analyst



Key responsibilities

 - Use AI to drive faster and better analysis and to automate systems

 - Run first-pass analysis on customer acquisition, conversion, and retention metrics

 - Turn findings into clear, simple summaries for commercial, marketing, and product teams

 - Learn Quantum's analytics practices and data stack, building toward owning your own areas



About you

 - A recent or upcoming degree in a maths or science based subject

 - A genuine interest in data and the commercial decisions it drives, with some hands-on exposure to Excel or SQL through study, a placement, or personal projects

 - AI native with demonstrable examples of how you’ve used AI as a student, on a work placement or privately

 - Curious by nature, keen to understand why the numbers move the way they do

 - Strong written and verbal communication, able to articulate complex ideas and explain findings in simple terms

 - Organised and reliable, able to manage your own tasks and hit deadlines

 - You thrive when working as part of a team

 - Comfortable in a fast-paced environment

 - Have excellent written and verbal English skills

 - • Last but not least, you'll have no ego!

JLL empowers you to shape a brighter way .

 What this job involves:    
 Our graduate programme will provide you with first-hand experience while working towards a professional qualification. 
 You’ll join us on a 2 – 3year trainee programme, working towards Project Management Chartered Surveyor status with the Royal Institute of Chartered Surveyors (RICS). 
 If you do not have an RICS accredited Real Estate degree, you will complete a fully funded online master's degree (MSc) in Construction Management with the University of the Built Environment as part of the graduate programme. You will be fully supported by both JLL and the University throughout your academic journey.   
 The PMO Graduate role offers an exciting opportunity to launch your career within a dynamic professional services environment. You will support the delivery of complex programmes, gaining hands-on experience in programme governance, reporting, and stakeholder management while developing essential skills in programme management best practices. 
 Key Responsibilities:  
 Project Support & Coordination:  Support the PMO team in coordinating project activities across multiple workstreams, ensuring alignment with programme objectives and timelines. Assist in scheduling meetings, tracking action items, and maintaining project documentation to ensure smooth programme execution. 
 Reporting & Documentation: Prepare programme status reports, dashboards, and presentations for various stakeholder groups. Maintain accurate project records, including risk registers, issue logs, and dependency trackers. Support the development and maintenance of programme documentation and templates. 
 Data Analysis & Performance Tracking: Collect, analyse, and present programme data to monitor progress against key performance indicators. Support the identification of trends, risks, and opportunities for improvement. Assist in creating visualizations and metrics that enable effective decision-making. 
 Stakeholder Engagement:  Work collaboratively with various teams, business units, and external partners to gather information and coordinate activities. Support stakeholder communications and help facilitate workshops or working sessions as required. 
 Process Improvement:  Contribute to the continuous improvement of PMO processes, tools, and methodologies. Help identify opportunities to enhance efficiency and effectiveness in programme delivery. 
 What you’ll get from us:  
 We know that your unique backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives help us think bigger, spark innovation and succeed together. 
 At JLL, we want everyone to feel welcomed, valued, and empowered to achieve their full potential, and here are just some of the ways we’ll make that happen. 
 Support from us – The Early Careers team will be with you every step of the way during your programme. Your manager and team will also be there to guide you day-to-day.

About Us : 
 Founded more than 15 years ago and headquartered in Chicago, the DV Group of financial services firms has grown to more than 600 people operating throughout North America and in Europe. Since spinning out of a large brokerage firm in 2016, DV Trading has rapidly scaled as an independent proprietary trading firm utilizing its own capital, trading strategies, and risk management methodologies to provide liquidity to worldwide financial markets and hedging opportunities to commodity producers and users. Now, DV group affiliates include two broker dealers, a cryptocurrency market making firm, and a bourgeoning investment adviser. 
 DV Commodities is a division within DV Group that specializes in trading commodities markets, including crude oil, refined products, natural gas, power, emissions, metals, softs, and agriculture. DV Commodities' risk management, world-class technology, and talented traders have enabled it to become one of the world’s largest liquidity providers and risk allocators in the energy and commodities spaces. DV Commodities currently has over 35 desks, with traders and staff located in London, New York, Chicago, Houston, and Dubai.
 Overview:
 As a Trading Intern, you'll work closely with our teams to learn about different types of trading strategies, ranging from Market Making in Oil Products to Fundamental Discretionary approaches in European Gas & Power. We aim to have you rotate on at least 2 desks to give you the chance to explore what trading style fits best with your skill set. You will be asked to build and maintain applications that assist trading activities, whether it is through the creation of new Analytics Dashboards or novel ideas which you back-test and present to us. 
 You will be mentored by both senior and junior traders, with constant exposure to senior leadership. We foster a culture that encourages cross desk cooperation. If you want to understand how we navigate trading a wide range of commodities markets, this internship is an exciting opportunity. Strong intern candidates are considered for full time roles upon graduation. 
 Requirements: 
 Currently pursuing a degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, Engineering or a related field and graduating by Summer 2027 or Summer 2028 
 Strong interest in trading and model development

 Junior Client Portfolio Manager 
 Ebury London Victoria office - Onsite 
 We are offering an exciting opportunity to join a fast growing team in London. You will take on a book of corporate clients, providing daily operational and trading assistance as well as building relationships and upselling Ebury's products. You’ll have a combination of client-facing skill/experience, operational know-how and problem-solving abilities. You’ll be servicing the revenue and growth area of the business at an exciting time for the company. You will act as an ambassador for the product and service at a customer-facing level.

904cf676a8c8.title: IT Operations Systems Assistant
904cf676a8c8.description:
Reports to: People Manager / Operations team

Location: London / UK preferred (hybrid — office access is a bonus, not required)



Company Overview:

Radiant is redefining how AI infrastructure is built.

We design and operate AI-native cloud platforms engineered for sovereignty, performance, and scale. Our infrastructure powers GPU-native workloads, multi-tenant control planes, and high-performance AI systems designed for the most demanding environments.

We are not building a generic cloud. We are building purpose-built AI infrastructure — from powered land, to compute, to software.

As we scale, we're building this organisation from the ground up. We're looking for people who'd rather build the playbook than inherit one — who are comfortable doing the work themselves as well as directing others, and who can adapt as fast as our strategy does. This is a startup model: attitude and adaptability matter more to us than years of experience or the size of team you've previously managed.

This is a cross-functional role requiring strong technical, commercial, and delivery capabilities, with exposure to executive stakeholders and our EOR and benefits providers, regional legal and finance partners, and every hiring manager relying on one people function as we scale.

What You'll Do

You will provide day-to-day operational and technical support across Radiant's IT systems, hardware, and end users. The role acts as a first point of contact for IT support requests and plays a key part in keeping core systems, devices, and user accounts running smoothly, securely, and in line with company policies.

Key Responsibilities


SERVICE DESK AND USER SUPPORT

 - Act as first point of contact for IT support requests, logging, triaging, and resolving tickets, escalating to senior colleagues where appropriate


SYSTEMS AND ACCOUNT ADMINISTRATION

 - Administer user accounts through the joiner, mover, and leaver process, including account creation, permission changes, and timely deactivation of access

 - Assign and track software licences, ensuring allocations remain accurate and cost-effective


HARDWARE AND ASSET MANAGEMENT

 - Build, configure, and deploy laptops and mobile devices for new starters

 - Maintain an accurate IT asset register, tracking equipment from procurement through to secure disposal

 - Arrange repairs, replacements, and warranty claims with external suppliers


SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE

 - Perform periodic audits of systems access

 - Support day-to-day security practices, including multi-factor authentication setup, access reviews, and prompt removal of leaver access

 - Follow established IT policies and procedures, and flag risks, incidents, or recurring issues to senior colleagues

 - Handle accounts, access, and company data with care and in line with data protection obligations


DOCUMENTATION AND CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

 - Create and maintain knowledge base articles, user guides, and internal process documentation

 - Identify recurring issues and contribute suggestions to improve systems, processes, and the end-user experience

Qualities we look for:

 - Set the standard: Every single day, you spot opportunities to constructively shake things up.

 - Inspire the change: There's no blueprint for the future. You'll embrace challenges and change.

 - You're real and you're true to yourself: We cherish and celebrate diversity so you'll feel right at home whoever you are and whoever you're talking to, you treat everyone the same.

 - Get stuck in: You'd rather be building than overseeing. Our strategy will keep evolving, and so will you — attitude and adaptability matter more to us than a fixed playbook or a big team behind you.

7b0a3ec8c8a6.title: AI Technology PhD Research Internship
7b0a3ec8c8a6.location: Bristol, UK; Cambridge, UK; London, UK Bristol, Cambridge, London
7b0a3ec8c8a6.description:
Location: UK based from either our Bristol, Cambridge or London office.
 Research PhD Internship  
 Explore a research career at Graphcore through a PhD internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. You’ll bring fresh ideas, put your learning into practice and help shape what we’re creating. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence.
 What you’ll work on
 Explore how your research could inform the next generation of AI compute, working alongside researchers tackling questions shaped by real-world hardware and software challenges.
 Our team is interested in numerous topics across the field, working on problems where algorithms, hardware, and systems meet. These topics include large-scale pretraining and post-training of LLMs, efficient inference, numerics, world models, molecule generation for life science applications, and model safety and interpretability. Across all these directions, you’ll come up with new ideas, implement models and algorithms, design experiments, and present your findings (often in the form of a paper).
 You’ll have room to follow promising ideas and help shape your research direction, with mentoring as you test your thinking. Your work could contribute to public research shared with the wider AI community.
 Your team and support
 Graphcore Research explores the computational requirements of machine intelligence and how hardware can enable the next generation of AI models. The team publishes at leading AI and machine learning conferences, including NeurIPS, ICML and ICLR.
 You’ll learn alongside researchers working across a wide range of AI topics. Mentoring and open research discussions will give you opportunities to explore ideas, get feedback and decide which questions to pursue.
 Decisions are shaped by experimental evidence and technical discussion. As an intern, you’ll be encouraged to ask questions, challenge assumptions and share results early, with support from experienced researchers as you develop your ideas.
 How you’ll learn and grow
 Over the internship, you’ll build research experience by taking a question through experimentation, implementation and analysis.
 You’ll develop your judgement about what a result tells you, which ideas deserve further investigation and how to communicate your findings clearly. Exploring both theory and practical experiments will help you understand how your research connects to AI models, hardware and systems, and where you’d like to take it next.
 What we're looking for 
 Currently studying for a PhD specialising in AI or machine learning.
 Strong coding ability in Python or C++, demonstrated through projects, research or other practical experience
 Experience implementing algorithms in machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch
 The ability to design experiments, interpret results and communicate research clearly, with curiosity about both theory and practical experimentation
 Previous industry experience is not required. Tell us about a research question you explored, how you approached it and what you learned through your experiments.
 Benefits
 Flexible working: Find a balance between your internship and life outside work
 Life in the office: Get to know your colleagues in spaces designed for collaboration, with free food and a great selection of ice cream!
 Develop your research in an industry setting, exchanging ideas with experienced researchers and engineers
 We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.
 We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you.
 Sponsorship
 Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities.
 Introduction to Graphcore
 At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: from semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier.
 An internship at Graphcore gives you the chance to explore where your interests and skills could take you. You’ll work alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. Together, you’ll share ideas and solve challenging problems, building experience and confidence to help you decide what comes next.
 Curious about where your skills could take you? Apply for a PhD internship at Graphcore and help us build what comes next.

c1e4893d0fd8.title: Quantitative Researcher - 2027 Summer Internship
c1e4893d0fd8.location: Amsterdam, North Holland, Netherlands; London, England, United Kingdom; New York; Singapore Amsterdam, London, New York, Singapore
c1e4893d0fd8.description:
At Graviton, every strategy, model and edge begins not with instinct, but with someone asking a better question than everyone else.
 As a Quantitative Research Intern, you'll spend 10-12 weeks working on research that directly shapes how we understand markets and build trading strategies. You'll collaborate with researchers and technologists to investigate market behaviour, test hypotheses, build predictive models and solve problems where the answers aren't obvious.
 This isn't an internship where you observe from the sidelines. Outstanding work has the potential to shape production strategies and generate real, measurable returns.
 Ideal candidates are quantitatively sharp, practically minded problem solvers, programmers, mathematicians and scientists who are excited to solve the hardest problems in our field, across our offices in the US, Singapore, Amsterdam and London.
 What You'll Work On 
 You'll work on real research problems, not simulated exercises, discovering predictive patterns from billions of market events, designing statistical models, and applying machine learning to open research problems. Your work would include:
 Discovering predictive patterns from billions of market events
 Designing statistical models that identify trading opportunities
 Applying probability, optimization and machine learning to open research problems
 Building AI-powered research agents that accelerate experimentation
 Developing infrastructure for rapid, large-scale research
 Designing experiments and backtests to evaluate hypotheses
 Translating research into production-ready trading signals
 Exploring new ML, AI and quant finance techniques to find the next source of alpha
 What You'll Learn 
 Beyond the technical exposure, you'll learn how experienced researchers approach hard problems: breaking them down, questioning assumptions, and deciding based on evidence rather than intuition. You'll be paired with a mentor, reporting manager and buddy, with regular code reviews and feedback throughout the internship.
 What Success Looks Like 
 Successful interns leave having delivered a complete research project from hypothesis to evaluation, built statistically rigorous models, and demonstrated curiosity, ownership and the ability to solve open-ended problems.
 Who We're Looking For 
 We're looking for exceptional students who genuinely enjoy solving hard problems.
 Full-time undergraduate, Master's or PhD student in a quantitative discipline (math, physics, computer science, statistics, or a related field), graduating 2028
 Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++
 Grounded in probability, statistics, linear algebra and optimization, with experience in machine learning, statistical modelling or data analysis, whether through coursework, research or personal projects
 Comfortable working with large, complex datasets, with strong analytical thinking
 A passion for applying quantitative thinking and rigorous research to solve open-ended problems in markets
 Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly
 Our Culture 
 More than specific technologies, we care how you think. We look for people who are curious enough to question assumptions, analytical enough to separate signal from noise, persistent enough to keep searching past the first answer, humble enough to keep learning, and excited by problems without textbook solutions.
 At Graviton, researchers sit alongside engineers to solve problems where milliseconds matter and better models create real competitive advantage. You'll get meaningful ownership from day one, in a culture built on intellectual honesty and continuous improvement. Your contribution won't be measured by hours spent, but by the quality of your thinking.
 Markets are among the most complex systems humans have ever created. Every day, someone discovers a better answer. This summer, that someone could be you.

dcfef373d5b0.title: Quantitative Researcher - 2027 Graduates
dcfef373d5b0.location: Amsterdam, North Holland, Netherlands; London, England, United Kingdom; New York; Singapore Amsterdam, London, New York, Singapore
dcfef373d5b0.description:
At Graviton, we don't believe the best trading strategies come from following established playbooks. They come from asking better questions. Why does a pattern exist? What is driving it? Is it real or just noise? Can it be explained, modelled and turned into an edge?
 As a Quantitative Researcher, you'll work on those questions every day. You'll investigate market behaviour, develop quantitative models, build and test hypotheses and turn insights into trading strategies, working alongside researchers and technologists in an environment where an idea on a whiteboard can reach live trading quickly.
 This isn't a role where the answers are in a textbook. The problems are open-ended, the data is enormous, and finding the answers is the job.
 Ideal candidates are rigorous thinkers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious, based in our Singapore, London, Amsterdam or US offices.
 What You'll Work On
 You'll work across quantitative research and systematic trading, taking ideas through the full lifecycle: question, hypothesis, experiment, model, validation, strategy, production. Depending on your team and research interests, your work would include:
 Discovering predictive patterns and sources of alpha from billions of market events
 Formulating hypotheses about market behaviour and designing experiments to test them
 Applying probability, statistics, optimization and machine learning to build predictive models and quantitative signals for systematic trading
 Designing robust backtests and statistical tests to distinguish genuine signals from noise
 Working with large and complex datasets to uncover patterns that aren't immediately visible
 Investigating market microstructure and how markets behave at different timescales
 Evaluating strategy performance, identifying weaknesses and continuously refining models
 Developing research infrastructure and AI-powered tools and agents that make experimentation faster and analysis deeper
 Working closely with technologists to translate research ideas into efficient, production-ready systems
 Exploring new techniques in machine learning, statistics and quantitative finance to uncover new sources of edge
 No two research problems are the same. Good research finds patterns. Great research understands why they exist.
 What Success Looks Like
 Successful researchers at Graviton discover new sources of alpha and turn them into robust trading strategies, build models that hold up under real market conditions and not only in backtests, develop a deep understanding of market behaviour, create research frameworks and tools that make the broader team more effective, work with technologists to take ideas from research into production, and communicate complex quantitative ideas clearly and rigorously. Your impact isn't measured by how many models you build. It's measured by the quality of the ideas you discover and what those ideas enable.
 Who We're Looking For
 We're looking for exceptional problem solvers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious.
 Degree in a quantitative discipline such as mathematics, physics, computer science, statistics, operations research or machine learning
 No active backlogs
 Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++
 Solid grounding in probability, statistics, linear algebra and optimization, with experience in machine learning, statistical modelling or data analysis, whether through coursework, research or personal projects
 Comfort working with large, complex datasets, and strong analytical thinking
 A passion for applying quantitative thinking and rigorous research to solve open-ended problems in markets
 Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly
 Prior exposure to quantitative research, algorithmic trading, market microstructure, competitive mathematics or machine learning is valuable, but we care more about how you think than whether you've worked in finance before.
 Our Culture
 More than specific tools or techniques, we care how you think. We look for people who are curious enough to keep asking why, analytical enough to separate signal from noise, persistent enough to pursue difficult problems, intellectually honest enough to abandon an idea when the evidence says so, and humble enough to keep learning.
 At Graviton, researchers sit alongside technologists on specialized trading teams that operate with significant autonomy. You'll have meaningful ownership of research problems from day one: forming your own hypotheses, challenging existing approaches and following the evidence wherever it leads, with the infrastructure and datasets to test ideas at scale, competitive compensation, and a culture where the best idea wins regardless of who proposed it.
 Markets are among the most complex systems humans have ever created, and they never stop changing. Neither should our thinking. Every day, someone asks a better question and finds an answer nobody had. That someone could be you.

6aaadfd9d897.title: AI & Management Consulting Intern (Value Engineering - UKI Market)
6aaadfd9d897.location: London, United Kingdom London, United Kingdom
6aaadfd9d897.description:
Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.
 The Team: 
 As an Intern in AI & Management Consulting you join our Value Engineering team to focus on driving and closing opportunities by identifying and selling the value Celonis can bring to customers. Our Value Engineers (VE) are the trusted advisor for customers and work on the intersection of technology and business. Value Engineers partner with sales and customers to create compelling solutions to critical business problems. A great VE understands the customer, the technology, and the sales cycle making it what may be the most interesting, challenging, and fulfilling role in enterprise technology sales.
 The Role:
 Value Engineers are the trusted advisors for our prospects and customers and leverage product expertise and business acumen to solve our prospects’ and customers’ most pressing challenges. You will gain experience in executing proof of value projects and take part in technical discussions with stakeholders. By creating customer-based business cases, you support the strategic business development activities for the UKI market.
 The work you’ll do: 
 Analyze data from our customers to increase transparency in business processes
 Understand the pain points of our customers and translate them into actionable use cases in the Celonis Process Intelligence Platform
 Collaborate with customers and partners to uncover their core business challenges and determine how Celonis Process Intelligence can help them achieve their business objectives
 Quantify financial impact of use cases implemented in the Celonis Process Intelligence Platform and prepare management ready presentations
 Present findings together with your team in front of customers’ C-level and decision makers
 Leverage Celonis data modeling and AI capabilities to uncover process inefficiencies, generate insights, and deliver high impact, data driven value propositions to clients.
 Pitch the Celonis AI value proposition and vision to customers and align our solutions with their AI strategy
 Build strong relationships with our customers by winning their trust through technical, product expertise, and business acumen
 The qualifications you need: 
 Student of Business Informatics, Data Analytics/Science, Computer Science, Industrial Engineering, Technology & Management, Mathematics or of a comparable program
 Strong communicational skills and interest in interacting with potential customers
 Confidence to present to C-level executives and larger audiences
 Have a passion for technology, data, OpenAI and LLMs and the impact it can have on the world
 Experience in consulting and highly interested in Data Analytics
 Knowledge in SQL and Python or related database query languages (completion of Celonis "Rising Star" modules would be a plus)
 Analytical mindset and the ability to multi-task, prioritize and execute
 Effective communicator and business fluent in English (must). 
 Availability from October/ November onwards for at least five months. 
 Motivated to transition into a full-time role through the Orbit Graduate Program following a successful internship 
 What Celonis can offer you: 
 Pioneer Innovation: Work with the global leader in Process Mining and the Process Intelligence Graph to shape the future of AI-driven business operations.
 Ownership from Day 1: Every full-time "Celonaut" is an owner, receiving Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and merit-based refresh grants.
 Unrivaled Family Support: Benefit from our inclusive parental leave policy—24 weeks of fully paid leave for primary carers and 12 weeks for supporting carers, available from your first day of employment.
 Work-Life Integration: Enjoy Unlimited PTO (in applicable regions) and generous PTO globally, as well as a flexible hybrid work model that balances remote focus with vibrant office collaboration.
 Continuous Growth: Elevate your skills through our 70-20-10 learning framework, mentorship programs, and access to a dedicated learning platform.
 Holistic Well-being: Prioritize your health with subsidized Wellhub memberships, mental health counseling, and dedicated "Wellness Weeks" that prioritize work/life balance.
 Drive Sustainability: Participate in annual Impact Days, where you receive paid time off to volunteer for community and environmental causes with your local office, or virtually.
 Global Inclusion & Belonging: Find community through our Inclusion Think Tank and participate in our annual Inclusion Days, ensuring every voice is heard and valued.
 Value-Driven Impact: Join a mission-led organization where our core values—Live for Customer Value, The Best Team Wins, We Own It, and Earth Is Our Future—drive every decision.
 About Us: 
 Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI, empowering organizations to analyze, design, and operate AI-driven processes. The Celonis Platform is powered by the Celonis Context Model, which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence to create a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can understand — turning AI’s operational blind spots into operational clarity. Industry-leading companies around the world trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. Celonis is headquartered in Munich, Germany, and New York City, USA, with more than 20 offices worldwide.
 Get familiar with the Celonis Process Intelligence Platform by watching this video .
 Celonis Inclusion Statement: 
 At Celonis, we believe our people make us who we are and that “The Best Team Wins”. We know that the best teams are made up of people who bring different perspectives to the table. And when everyone feels included, able to speak up and knows their voice is heard - that's when creativity and innovation happen. 
 Your Privacy: 
 Any information you submit to Celonis as part of your application will be processed in accordance with Celonis’ Accessibility and Candidate Notices 
 By submitting this application, you confirm that you agree to the storing and processing of your personal data by Celonis as described in our Privacy Notice for the Application and Hiring Process .
 Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools 
We rely on an artificial intelligence tool to match the information from your resume to the relevant Celonis job descriptions. This processing is limited to the information provided in your resume or in your candidate profile. The tool produces a match score per candidate for a role, suggests preliminary ranking, and provides recommendations.
The tool is only used for support in parts of the job application process, including to facilitate the identification of the relevant Celonis Jobs for candidates and recruiters. All final decisions are made by hiring managers and the Celonis talent acquisition team. Hiring managers and HR specialists use this tool responsibly, are aware of the risk of potential bias, and are equipped to mitigate it.
 Please be aware of common job offer scams, impersonators and frauds. Learn more here .

 Who we are: 
 Rothesay is the UK’s largest pensions insurance specialist, purpose-built to protect pension schemes and their members’ pensions. With over £74 billion of assets under management, we secure the pensions of more than one million people and pay out, on average, approximately £350 million in pension payments each month.
 Rothesay is dedicated to providing excellence in customer service alongside prudent underwriting, a conservative investment strategy and the careful management of risk. We are trusted by the pension schemes of some of the UK’s best known companies to provide pension solutions, including British Airways, Cadbury, the Civil Aviation Authority, the Co-Operative, Morrisons, Smiths Industries and Telent. At Rothesay, we are striving to transform our industry. We believe deeply in creating real security for the future and our leadership in finding new and better ways to do that is the key to our success. To do that, we need the very brightest original thinkers to bring creativity as well as rigour. Rothesay is a rewarding place to work, where quality people can thrive and prosper.  Graduate Programme: 
 Our UK graduate programme is designed to kick-start careers for ambitious and analytical graduates who want to make an impact. Rothesay is built on a multi-talented, multi-disciplined model, collaborating directly and with singular focus to shape the future. Rothesay’s inclusive and collaborative working environment allows our graduates to build a broad skill-set and shape a strong internal network. We support your development journey, growth in your career, in addition to offering a competitive salary and tailored benefits.
 Our 2 year* programme starts with a fundamentals week for the entire graduate cohort, where you will have in depth networking and insight sessions on Rothesay as a whole. From week two, you will join your team for professional integrated learning and start to make meaningful contributions. Throughout your first year, alongside your permanent role, you will be part of an on-site graduate development programme with both technical and business skills training.  Our teams run lean, giving you excellent visibility and exposure throughout the business, and we will provide continuous training and upskilling for your future.  Rothesay is a rewarding place to work, where quality people can thrive and prosper.  Regular reviews will take place to support your learning and development with a formal assessment towards the end of the programme.
 This opportunity is open to summer 2027 graduates who are looking to launch into their career within an entrepreneurial environment where talent can thrive and excel.
 What you’ll do:

Discover your future at Citi 
Working at Citi is far more than just a job. A career with us means joining a team of approximately 219,000 dedicated people from around the globe. At Citi, you'll have the opportunity to grow your career, give back to your community and make a real impact. 
 Job Overview 
 You're the brains behind our work. 
You're ready to bring your knowledge from the classroom to the boardroom, and Citi wants to help you get there. Whether it's honing your skills or building your network, we know that success can't come without growth. Our programs equip you with the knowledge and training you need to play a valuable role on your team and establish a long-term career here. At Citi, we value internal mobility, and career growth is not a question of if, but when. Citi's Internal Audit Group is looking for Summer Analysts to join the team in London. Citi's Internal Audit division provides independent assessments of the company's governance, risk management and internal control environment for key stakeholders including the Board of Directors, senior management and Citi's numerous regulators globally. Internal Audit is a change agent within Citi aimed to enhance the control culture of Citi worldwide and thereby support senior management decision making around the globe. 
 We provide you with the knowledge and skills you need to succeed. 
Citi's Internal Audit Summer Analyst Program is a 10-week internship opportunity in London. This Program will provide development-focused opportunities coupled with structured classroom training, mentoring and individual development. As an Internal Audit Summer Analyst, you will face off into one of Citi's core businesses or global functions to ensure that a sound control framework and environment is in place globally through the delivery of independent and timely assurance. 
 Your time here will look something like this... 
The Internal Audit Summer Analyst program begins in June with a 3-day training program, providing Summer Analysts with an overview of Citi and an introduction to Citi's Internal Audit Organization. The Summer Program will provide Summer Analysts with Senior and Junior Mentors, networking opportunities and Senior Speaker Events where Citi's senior IA professionals will host discussions and answer questions about their careers and IA functions. Most opportunities will require and enable cross-functional exposure, giving candidates a well-rounded experience at Citi. The Summer Analysts will receive real-world work and will be expected to add value to their teams during the 10 weeks. In addition to their daily work, the Summer Analysts will also have the opportunity to network with other Citi interns, current program participants, and other IA professionals. The program concludes with the Summer Analysts presenting their accomplishments and lessons learned to the Senior IA Management team. Top performing Summer Analysts will be considered for the full-time Internal Audit Analyst Programs. 
 We want to hear from you if...

 Graduating in summer 2027 and on track for a 2.1 or equivalent.

• Strong Analytical skills
